---
title: "Majority comparisons and expected ranks"
subtitle: "1.15 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 10, and Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), section II.F"
description: "Relation between majority-win counts, posterior-mean rankings and expected ranks."
---

Counting pairs a unit more likely wins matches posterior-mean order under independent normal posteriors, yet diverges from expected rank and general laws.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Law on orders.** A wins two pairs (.51 each); B's .99 win puts B first by expected rank (1.52 vs. 1.98).
- **League.** Majority wins match posterior means (0 of the 435 pairs differ); expected rank reverses 6 pairs (U13: 8th, 9.59 vs. 6th).
- **League, prior SD .30.** Majority wins and posterior means differ on 0 of the 435 pairs; expected rank reverses 12 pairs.
- **KRW, race.** Posterior mean reverses 35 of the 4,656 pairs (1,249 wrong) and expected rank 62; λ = 1 card reverses none (1,248).
- **KRW, gender.** Macy's (.5008), Jones Lang LaSalle (.502), and Dollar General (.5014) cycle at 45 pairs each; the card uses 96 grades.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Data: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC, noncommercial use only (`pr_case_krw`; [KRW's cards along λ](../cases/krw-lambda.qmd)). No endorsement is implied. **Data describe KRW's experiment, not current conduct.**
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank); r <- pr_case_krw$alternatives$race; e <- r$e[, , 1]
w <- rowSums(e < t(e), na.rm = TRUE); pm <- postrank_posterior_means(r)[, 1]; er <- postrank_expected_rank(r)
c(mean = sum(outer(w, w, ">") & outer(pm, pm, "<")), rank = sum(outer(w, w, ">") & outer(er, er, ">")))   # 35 62
```
:::
